leads.title: Republic Act 9048 - Clerical Error Law of 2001
leads.documents: National ban on changing sex marker in birth certificates without judicial order; states 'no correction must involve the change of nationality, age, status or sex'
leads.detail: Cited as 'The Clerical Error Law of 2001 (RA 9048)' in Gender identity and expression section; no URL visible in text

leads.title: Revised Penal Code of the Philippines, Article 200 - Grave Scandal
leads.documents: Criminal provision that can apply to public same-sex conduct/affection; penalty of arresto mayor and public censure for highly scandalous conduct offending decency
leads.detail: Quoted verbatim: 'ARTICLE 200. Grave Scandal.—The penalties of arresto mayor and public censure...' in Laws regarding same-sex sexual activity section

leads.title: Family Code of the Philippines; House Bill 1015 Civil Partnership Act and Senate Bill 449 Civil Unions Act (19th Congress)
leads.documents: Non-recognition of same-sex marriage/civil unions - only marriages between 'a man and a woman'; shows pending civil union proposals by Rep. Bernadette Herrera and Senate
leads.detail: Cited in Recognition of same-sex relationships section; Constitution noted as silent on same-sex unions

leads.title: SOGIE Equality Bill / Anti-Discrimination Bill
leads.documents: National anti-discrimination bill status - passed House Sept 20, 2017 198-0 after 17 years, stalled/died in Senate in 17th Congress June 2019; proposed fines P100,000-500,000 and 1-6 years imprisonment
leads.detail: Introduced by Hon. Kaka J. Bag-ao July 1, 2013; principal Senate author Risa Hontiveros; opposition/support senators named; reintroduced by Sonny Angara July 2019

leads.title: Marawi City Council Ordinance December 2004; Kabacan, Cotabato Ordinance November 2019
leads.documents: Local enforcement criminalizing trans expression - Marawi bans men wearing female attire/makeup/earrings as part of Islamic 'cleaning and cleansing'; Kabacan prohibits cross-dressing and homosexual relations for Muslims with penalty of imprisonment
leads.detail: Marawi mayor's 'cleaning and cleansing drive' quote; Kabacan applies to Muslims; also noted murders/harassment of trans persons post-2017 Marawi siege

leads.title: Supreme Court of the Philippines - gender marker and marriage rulings
leads.documents: Court rulings on gender/sexuality - affirmed lower court change of gender legal marker due to intersex status; 2025 ruling that concealment of homosexuality from spouse is fraud ground for annulment
leads.detail: Cited in Gender identity section and Contemporary section 'In 2025, the Supreme Court... ruled'; no case number/URL visible

leads.title: Executive Order No. 51 signed Dec 22, 2023 by President Bongbong Marcos
leads.documents: Rights machinery - establishes Special Committee on Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, Queer, Intersex, and Asexual Affairs; reconstitutes interagency committee on diversity and inclusion; LGUs encouraged to support
leads.detail: Cited as reinforcing national Diversity and Inclusion Program; department secretaries to lead

leads.title: Department of Education Gender-Responsive Basic Education Policy July 2017; DSWD uniform policy 2016
leads.documents: Government policy on gender identity in schools - curriculum review for gender stereotypes including LGBTQ-based, June as Pride Month observance; 2016 DSWD/Sec. Judy Taguiwalo allowed uniforms matching gender identities
leads.detail: July 2017 implementation date cited; joint DSWD-DepEd policy late 2016

leads.title: Being LGBT in Asia: The Philippines Country Report - USAID and UNDP
leads.documents: Institutional human-rights report documenting 1970s-1990s emergence of LGBT movement, Western influence on gay identity, Ladlad (1993), A Different Love (1994), first Pride March June 26, 1994, MCC 1991, UP Babaylan 1992, ProGay 1993, LAGABLAB 1999
leads.detail: Repeatedly cited as 'Based on a report made by USAID, in partnership with UNDP, entitled Being LGBT in Asia: The Philippines Country Report'

leads.title: ASEAN SOGIE Caucus Report November 2017; Human Rights Watch on June 26, 2020 Manila Pride arrests
leads.documents: ASEAN report documents shift to openness and 20+ local anti-discrimination ordinances but only Quezon City and Cebu City have IRR; HRW documents enforcement incident - police arrested ~20 Pride marchers in Manila charged under various laws despite social distancing, accused government of using COVID-19 to crack down
leads.detail: ASEAN report released in time for ASEAN Summit; HRW accusation quoted in Contemporary section; Quezon City Right to Care Card June 2023 praised by Philippine Commission on Human Rights also noted
